# Drawer

```tsx
import { Drawer, DrawerTrigger, DrawerClose, DrawerContent, DrawerHeader, DrawerTitle, DrawerBody, DrawerFooter } from "@lucasdost/design-system"
```

A panel that slides in from an edge of the screen over the page.

## Example

From the Storybook story; names like `args` or `label` are the story controls.

```tsx
<Drawer
  {...args}
  onOpenChange={(open, details) => {
    updateArgs({ open })
    args.onOpenChange?.(open, details)
  }}
>
  <DrawerTrigger render={<Button variant="secondary" />}>
    Open drawer
  </DrawerTrigger>
  <DrawerContent side={side}>
    <DrawerHeader showCloseButton={showCloseButton}>
      <DrawerTitle>{title}</DrawerTitle>
    </DrawerHeader>
    <DrawerBody>
      {Array.from({ length: paragraphs }, (_, index) => (
        <p key={index} className="text-text-secondary">
          Paragraph {index + 1}. Long content scrolls inside the body
          while the header and footer stay in place.
        </p>
      ))}
    </DrawerBody>
    {actions > 0 && (
      <DrawerFooter>
        {actions >= 3 && (
          <Button
            variant="ghost"
            danger={destructive === "ghost"}
            className="mr-auto"
          >
            Action 3
          </Button>
        )}
        {actions >= 2 && <Button variant="secondary">Action 2</Button>}
        <Button danger={destructive === "primary"}>Action 1</Button>
      </DrawerFooter>
    )}
  </DrawerContent>
</Drawer>
```

## Figma notes

Mirrors the Figma Drawer: a 460px side panel with Header (Title + close), a scrolling Body (the Slot) and an optional Footer (.Actions Footer).

## Props

Documented props only; every component also accepts the props of the element or Base UI part it renders (`className`, events, ARIA…).

`DrawerContent`:

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `side?` | `"top" \| "right" \| "bottom" \| "left"` | Figma shows the right side; the other edges reuse the same styles. |

## Rules

- Import `Drawer` from `@lucasdost/design-system`. Do not rebuild it with plain HTML and Tailwind classes.
- Style it through its props and variants first. Use `className` only for layout (margin, width, grid placement), never to change its colors, typography or radius.
- Colors come from the S0L tokens; see [color](../foundations/color.md).
